Tab renders both Account Detail and Cashflow cards, 37 lifetime year rows + 10 heir rows populate with dollar values (no all-dash rows), Net Worth column populated for every lifetime row (37/37 $ values, 0 dashes), heir rows visually shaded orange (#FBF7F0), both CSV exports trigger real browser downloads (account_detail.csv, cashflow.csv), and switching across all 5 tabs (optimizer→projection→cashflow→inputs→scenarios) works without crashes. action_items: Low-priority cleanup: in DetailCashflow.jsx replace bare <> fragments inside .map((g) => ...) with <Fragment key={g.type}>...</Fragment> (3 occurrences at lines ~97-102, ~110-115, ~124-129). This silences the React 'each child in a list should have a unique key prop' console warning. Does NOT affect rendering/functionality.

Low-priority polish: cashflow cell render uses `{v ? num(v) : '—'}` (line 171). A legitimate value of 0 is falsy and would render as '—' rather than '$0'. Recommend `{v == null ? '—' : num(v)}` to match the Account Detail helper. Not currently visible because backend appears to send null for empty rows, but is a latent inconsistency.
critical_code_review_comments: DetailCashflow.jsx uses unkeyed React fragments (<>...</>) as the top-level element returned from .map((g) => ...) calls inside both <thead> and <tbody>. This produces a 'missing key' console warning on every render. Replace with `<Fragment key={g.type}>` (and import { Fragment } from 'react').
Cashflow cell: `{v ? num(v) : '—'}` falsy-renders 0 as '—'. Use null-check (`v == null`) to align with num() helper and avoid hiding a legitimate $0 value.

useEffect dependency `[scenario]` on line 22 — since `scenario` is a brand-new object reference whenever the parent rerenders, the projection will refire even when the underlying data is unchanged. Consider a stable signature (JSON.stringify, or a hash field) to avoid duplicate /api/project calls every time the user mouses over a control elsewhere in the page.

Heir row per-account cells render '—' literal text; this is correct functionally but a tiny tooltip ('individual accounts merged at second death') would help non-spreadsheet users understand why those cells are blank.

rca of the issue: n/a — no defects. Key-prop warning RCA: DetailCashflow.jsx returns shorthand fragments <> from inside `.map((g) => ...)` callbacks; React requires the top-level node returned from a map to carry a key. Fix: import Fragment from 'react' and use `<Fragment key={g.type}>...</Fragment>` (or, simpler, wrap in a real DOM element/array). Three occurrences to update.
